newsitem.title: BELGIUM: FOCUS-Belgian Cera buys one bank, mulls pacts.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Belgian Cera buys one bank, mulls pacts.

text.p: Cera Bank, Belgium's sixth largest bank, on Friday continued its ambitious expansion drive, buying a small Swiss bank and announcing it was in talks with a number of other Belgian and foreign banks.
The bank is going for growth and cooperation pacts to prepare itself for the expected launch of Europe's single currency in 1999 and the increased competition that will entail.
It is also seeking economies of scale, bidding to keep costs down and margins intact.
"We are holding exploratory talks with a number of domestic and foreign banks but we do not want to put any names on them...everybody's talking with everyone," a spokesman said.

Belgian newspapers on Friday quoted Dutch Rabobank chairman Herman Wijffels as telling Thursday's annual meeting of local member bank representatives that the co-operative bank was in talks with Kredietbank (KB) and Cera.
KB, Belgium's third-largest bank, said last month it was in exploratory talks with Rabobank as part of expansion plans.

Rabobank, the Netherlands' number one in terms of balance sheet total, said in May it had been holding talks over the past year with KB about the unification of European markets, the single currency and globalisation of world financial markets.
It denied then the banks wanted to forge a close alliance.

Spokesman Jan Dos said on Friday Rabobank could undertake a joint venture with Kredietbank and Cera but it ruled out a merger. "There will never be a merger....but...activities we could jointly undertake could be put in a joint entity."

Dos said activities in which the banks could cooperate included private banking and investment banking. Talks were at an early stage. "These are investigative talks only. There have been no decisions by us or others."
Cera and Rabobank are members of a Europe-wide body of cooperative banks.

Cera, meanwhile, struck out on its own, announcing it bought Swiss Inca Bank SA, and thus continuing an expansion drive which includes the imminent closure of the takeover of Banque Indosuez Belgium and this autumn's opening of its first office in the Netherlands, in the border town of Maastricht.
Inca, specialising in private banking, based in Geneva and with a representative office in Zurich, will be renamed Cera Bank (Suisse) SA/Cera Bank (Schweiz) AG from July 1.

A Cera spokesman declined to give the purchase price. "That is not usual." Inca fitted in with Cera's strategy, which was to start developing private banking in Switzerland. Inca would act as a base for that, he said.

Unlisted Cera, with 1996 net consolidated profit of 5.78 billion francs and a balance sheet total of 1,304 billion francs, had said in March it was planning an acquisition in Switzerland before the summer.
Cera said at the time it would open additional branches in the Netherlands if Maastricht met its expectations.
In the past five years profits at the bank, which employs 4,573 people, has 939 offices and subsidiaries in Luxembourg, the Netherlands and the U.S., more than doubled.
Inca, with a balance sheet total of 11 million Swiss francs and assets under management worth 125 million Swiss francs, was previously majority-owned by business man Gaetan Carnaut.
A Cera spokesman declined to say whether Inca was profitable.
